about: Documents' tools for agents (through Agent Link): name, what it does, its arguments as JSON Schema, its group, whether it changes the document.

drawing_make.description: A drawing of bodies as a normal TechDraw page, editable in TechDraw (its template and title block, its views, section and dimensions), laid out in one call: standard views (front, top, right, iso by default; back, bottom, left too), first-angle (ISO) or third-angle (ASME) projection (left out: TechDraw's own preference, else third angle with inch units, else first; the answer says which and why), at the largest standard scale (1:1, 2:1, 1:2 …) that fits A4 or A3 with room for the dimensions and fills the sheet at most about 70% (the smallest paper at that scale; the iso view at its own scale where it has less room), clear of the template's title block; overall sizes dimensioned once each, outside the views, 10 mm off the outline (dimensions: false leaves them off), hidden: true dashes the hidden edges. Exports SVG, PDF and DXF to the output folder: the page's own TechDraw exports where TechDraw can write them (PDF and SVG need FreeCAD's window), Workshop's sheet writer for the rest (filesFrom says which); page: false writes the files only. dims adds feature dimensions with tolerances or ISO 286 fits (limits written in), holes calls out every round hole, grouped by size and how it is made ("4× ⌀8 THRU ⌴⌀13 ↧8.5"), with a leader in a view that sees it end on (front, right, top …), and lists the ones no drawn view sees end on in a hole table on the sheet; titleBlock fills the template's title block (TechDraw's ISO 5457 template; its sample names and numbers emptied, never a name made up; the date today, the scale and tolerance filled). section: a straight view drawn as a full section (cut square to it through the middle, sectionAt mm towards the viewer; the cut faces hatched, the cutting line lettered sectionLabel, A, in a view that sees it edge on) — for bores, pockets and walls inside. The dims and hole callouts go on the TechDraw page itself as TechDraw's own dimensions, each on its own: one TechDraw cannot take is listed under page.notOnPage by its view and text (item, why), never at the cost of the others or of the overall sizes already listed there. Each overall size is measured by TechDraw between the ends of drawn edges at the view's extremes (never a circle's or arc's centre, which TechDraw also keeps as a vertex), the next pair that measures the size tried if the extremes do not, kept only within 0.05 mm of the part's size. Each hole is found among the view's circles by its radius at the view's scale and its centre as the view projects it about the part's centre (TechDraw centres the part there); a callout whose place matches no circle goes on the view's circle of that size nearest it, with a warning to check it is the hole meant. Every view's lines are worked out (TechDraw does it on another thread) before any dimension goes on it and again before the export: page.viewsReadyIn says how long that took, page.viewsNotReady names any view still not drawn after 30 s; the page is never exported while one is not, and its SVG is checked to hold the views' lines (page.viewsInExport: drawn elements, template's, dimensions, the views' edges), exported once more after a further wait when it does not, and neither SVG nor PDF taken from the page when it still does not (filesFrom says why). Before the page's SVG and PDF are exported (TechDraw draws them from the scene of the page's tab, whose views' lines exist only once the tab has been shown and painted), the page is shown as a tab, that tab made the active one and painted, every view asked to repaint (no recompute) and the event loop run; page.exportScene lists the steps done (show, activate, paint, redraw, process), page.exportSceneAgain those before the second export. On the sheet writer's files a hole callout's leader lands only on a drawn circle of the hole's size (within 2%; a thread's tap drill accepted) where the hole projects in that view; a hole with none there (hidden in that view, or drawn otherwise) is left off the sheet, never put on another round edge such as a slot's end or a bore of another size, and listed under calloutsOff (view, label, why) and in its holes row (calloutOff). Hole callouts are kept apart: each one's text (at the sheet's size and at the page's, 3.5 mm, with a margin) clear of the views, the texts and every earlier callout, its leaders crossing no earlier leader nor running through an earlier text, raised 6 mm a try, on either side, at 45, 30 or 60 degrees.

bodies.description: Bodies to draw; all when left out.

projection.description: first (ISO) or third (ASME). Left out: TechDraw's preference (General ▸ projection angle), else third with inch units, else first.

scale.description: 0.5 for 1:2, 2 for 2:1; left out, the largest standard one that fits.

file.description: Where the files go: a name (in the session's folder), or a path — absolute (its folder made) or under the session's folder; an extension given is dropped, and the PDF, SVG and DXF share the stem.

dims.description: Feature dimensions: [{ view, kind: length (a, b, along h|v, offset mm) | diameter | radius (a round edge), fit "H7" or plus/minus mm, label }]; a and b a point [x,y,z] or a query { body, kind, type, radius, near } (a circle's centre, an edge's middle).

holes.description: true: every round hole called out in a view that sees it end on (front, right, top …), grouped by size: "4× ⌀3.4"; FreeCAD's own Holes as made ("2× ⌀6.6 THRU ⌴⌀11 ↧6.4", a thread's size); holes no drawn view sees end on in a hole table. Or a view's name: only that view's.

holeFits.description: A fit per hole diameter for the callouts: { "6": "H7" }.

titleBlock.description: { title, partNumber, revision, material, finish, drawnBy, date, checkedBy, company, generalTolerance (ISO 2768-m to start) } — filled into TechDraw's title block (and the files' own); ask the person for theirs.

drawing_exploded.description: An assembly manual: steps [{ title, add: [bodies], note }] in the order the parts go together; each step an isometric view (SVG) with the parts already in place and the new ones moved off by explode mm (up over their places, or out from the middle), a trail to where each goes and a balloon with its item number. Writes the steps and <name>_assembly.md with a bill of materials (bodies the same shape are one item, with the material and mass where part_spec recorded one, and how each is made from its setup). A body goes in once. Where the parts are in a FreeCAD Assembly, the moves also become the Assembly's own Exploded View (step k's parts k − 1 explode lengths up, or out from step 2 on), editable there, and an ordinary TechDraw page of it with a balloon per item and the bill of materials (page: false leaves the page out); outside an Assembly route says the steps use Workshop's own exploded shapes.

page.description: A TechDraw page of the Assembly's Exploded View (true by default; in an Assembly only).

patent_figures.description: Patent-style figures FIG. 1 … (iso, front, top, right by default): black line art on A4 within the USPTO's margins, no hidden lines or shading, each part's reference numeral (10, 20, 30 … or numerals { body: n }) with a lead line to a face of it the viewer sees. Writes an SVG and PDF per figure and a list of the numerals. A part hidden behind others in a view gets no numeral there (notSeenIn). Each figure is also an ordinary TechDraw page in that style (blank template, visible lines only, numerals as TechDraw balloons without a bubble), editable in TechDraw; its PDF and SVG are the page's exports where TechDraw can write them (filesFrom), else Workshop's sheet writer. page: false writes the files only.

bodies.description: Bodies to draw; all when left out.

page.description: Each figure as a TechDraw page too (true by default).

patent_draft.description: A Markdown draft of a patent description and a claims skeleton from the bodies — their sizes, which adjoin which, the numerals and figures of the last patent_figures — marked as a starting point for a patent attorney's review, with what only the inventor and counsel can say left in brackets. Written to the output folder; never filed or sent anywhere.

library_pack.description: Pack bodies to share: a zip of each as STEP and STL (formats), a README with their sizes, material and mass, and the print settings from their print setup (magnet pauses too), a LICENSE (license: CC-BY-4.0, CC-BY-SA-4.0, CC0-1.0 or MIT — ask the person; author is required for all but CC0), and credits [{ title, author, url, license, changes }] for remixed parts, refused when their licence does not allow the one chosen (no-derivatives, non-commercial, share-alike). The STEP header carries the file's name and the author given, no path, user name or organisation. When ScanRuler-FreeCAD is installed its pack makes it (through Agent Link's library_pack service), Documents' own otherwise; by says which (provider: documents for Documents' own).

provider.description: auto (ScanRuler's pack when installed, else Documents') or documents.
